title: Area decomposition and shaded complements
transcript: An area measures how many square units fill a region. Draw an extra line to split a complicated shape into pieces whose areas you can find. If the missing pieces are simpler, start with a whole rectangle and subtract them. Check whether those missing parts overlap.

AMC practice may shade the part left after one or more cuts. Compare the shaded region with an easy surrounding shape. A Rossmoyne style area problem may make regions overlap. Count a shared piece exactly once when subtracting or adding.
Join a six by five rectangle to a three by four rectangle along an edge without overlap. Find their combined area. A shared edge has length but contributes no extra area.
The first area is thirty and the second is twelve. No unit square belongs to both interiors. The areas add to forty-two square units. Joining along an edge leaves this total unchanged.
An eleven-by-nine rectangle has a right triangle removed from one corner. The perpendicular legs of the triangle are five and four units. Find the area left after that corner is removed.
The whole rectangle has area ninety-nine. The right triangle is half of a rectangle with sides five and four. Subtract the triangle. That leaves eighty-nine square units.

On a ten by nine board, shade a lower-left rectangle seven columns wide and six rows high. Shade the rectangle covering all columns from the fourth onwards and rows from the third upwards, with rows numbered from the bottom. How much area is unshaded?

The two shaded areas separately are forty-two and forty-nine. Adding them directly would count the shared part twice. The overlap has width four and height four. Its area is sixteen. Subtract the total shaded area from the full board. The overlap correction makes the unshaded area fifteen square units.

Check by counting the unshaded bottom right block and the unshaded top left block. Their areas are six and nine. Those two unshaded blocks have disjoint interiors. Their sum confirms the calculation using the overlap.

Area uses square units. Follow the interior and do not substitute the length around the edge for the covered region. When subtracting both shaded rectangles, one subtraction removes the overlap again. Add that common area back once.

Draw the full surrounding shape. Name each piece you add or subtract, and label its needed lengths. Check the intersection of any parts you counted separately. Add a second calculation if a different split is easy.
